locator: Abstract and sections 1.2, 1.3 and 7.

limitations: These bounds do not supply distribution-free polynomial-time improper learning; author spelling follows the inspected header.

title: Scott Analysis below the Vaught Ordinal
locator: Introduction before section 1; sections 3 and 4.
supports: Classical and infinitary Vaught conjectures remain open; recent progress restricts hypothetical counterexamples and settles certain Ehrenfeucht cases.
limitations: The paper switches to the infinitary version after its opening discussion. The classical first-order and infinitary targets are recorded separately.

title: Part 1 of Martin's Conjecture for order-preserving and measure-preserving functions
locator: Version 3, section 1.1 formal statement; section 1.2 known cases.

limitations: Year is that of the inspected 2024 revision, subsequently cited as a 2025 publication. No unrestricted ZFC assertion is made.

title: Computable learning of natural hypothesis classes
locator: Dated 14 June 2025; section 1.3, page 5 and footnote 2.
supports: Sacks's degree-invariant intermediate c.e. operator question remains open; later Martin-conjecture results settle special cases.
limitations: The informal word natural is motivational; the indexed task uses the precise degree-invariant operator formulation.

title: Information Inequalities for Five Random Variables
locator: Abstract and section 1, pages 1–2.
supports: The entropy-region structure remains largely unknown from four variables onward.
limitations: Finite copy-lemma families and Shannon outer cones are not complete descriptions of the almost-entropic region.

title: Binary Deletion Channel Capacity to Within One Hundredth of a Bit
locator: Sections 1.2, 2, 12-14; Table 1.

title: The Log-Rank Conjecture: New Equivalent Formulations
locator: Abstract and introduction.
supports: The log-rank conjecture remains open; signed rectangle rank provides an equivalent formulation.
limitations: Boolean-matrix rank and ordinary deterministic communication are intended, not approximate rank or randomized communication.

title: Alphabet-Preserving Lifting for the Log-Rank Conjecture
locator: Abstract and introduction.

limitations: Preprint; the improved bound is not needed for the candidate's statement and is not treated as independently verified.

limitations: Fixed positive ε may affect running time; setting ε to zero is not licensed. The target includes nonnegative rational vertex weights.

locator: Main text: model definition, equation (9), Discussion; supplementary section 5.1.

locator: Particle Data Group 2025 update, chapter 89; sections 89.1–89.2.1.

locator: Particle Data Group 2025 update, chapter 27; section 27.1 and candidate/search sections.

title: Dark Energy
locator: Particle Data Group 2025 update, chapter 28; sections 28.2 and observational status.
supports: Distinguishing a cosmological constant, evolving energy and modified gravity through expansion and structure growth.

locator: Particle Data Group 2025 update, chapter 25; sections 25.1.2, 25.2.1 and 25.4.

locator: Version 1 submitted 18 June 2026; abstract, introduction and conclusions.

locator: §1.1; Definitions 2–4; §3 proportionality degree and §4 approximation guarantees, v1 (28 September 2026).

limitations: Preprint; the inspected definitions use fixed-priority tiebreaking. Zero unrestricted guarantees and parameter-dependent positive bounds are different statements. Publication and independent proof acceptance were not established.

title: On the Parallelizability of Approval-Based Committee Rules
locator: §1.1 Theorem 1; §§2.2–3. ECAI 2025 proceedings, publisher page first online August 25, 2026. Full manuscript: https://arxiv.org/html/2501.15006v2, dated May 9, 2025; Appendices A and C, especially C.4–C.5.
supports: Classifies the surveyed polynomial-time ABC rules: AV/SAV admit logspace computation, while the listed sequential rules are P-hard.
limitations: The full manuscript separates MES's first phase from MES completed by sequential Phragmén. The complexity conclusion uses the usual separation assumption; no arbitrary completion rule or practical speedup bound is covered. Proofs have not been independently reproduced.

title: Ties in Multiwinner Approval Voting
locator: Table 1 and §2, parallel-universes tiebreaking; §§3–4.

limitations: Uniqueness and counting are distinct from candidate- or committee-membership under some tiebreaking; these results cannot be transferred without a reduction.

title: Completeness theorem for the system of eigenfunctions of the complex Schrödinger operator L=-d²/dx²+cx^(2/3)
locator: Abstract; v2 (17 April 2019)

locator: Abstract and submission metadata.

title: Stronger Lower Bounds for (Non-)Anytime Acceleration of Gradient Descent
locator: Version 2, 4 September 2026; equation (1), Theorems 1.1-1.2 and Sections 3-5. Version date checked against the arXiv abstract page.

Section 5 leaves the upper/lower rate gap unresolved.
limitations: The stated lower bounds were read, not independently proved. The anytime theorem is a limsup obstruction, not a pointwise lower bound at every iteration.

title: Acceleration by stepsize hedging: Silver Stepsize Schedule for smooth convex optimization
locator: Mathematical Programming 213, 1105-1118; published online 25 November 2024, issue September 2025; DOI 10.1007/s10107-024-02164-2; Sections 1-3.
supports: Gives a deterministic silver stepsize schedule with objective-gap exponent log_2(1+sqrt(2)) at its terminal iterations.
Explains recursive composition of multi-step descent inequalities.
limitations: This is an upper-bound construction, not a proof that its rate is optimal. Special terminal iterations and anytime guarantees must be distinguished.

title: Anytime Acceleration of Gradient Descent
locator: COLT 2025, PMLR 291:5991-6013; conference 30 June-4 July 2025; publisher abstract and bibliography.
supports: Reports one predetermined infinite schedule with a last-iterate guarantee for every stopping time.
Its exponent is 2a/(1+a), where a=log_2(1+sqrt(2)); it resolves the earlier question of beating 1/T in the anytime setting.
limitations: Publisher abstract inspected; the full proof was not audited. The sharp anytime exponent remains a separate question.

limitations: Preprint; proof not independently audited. Publication chronology needs clarification. Tightness for maximum Nash welfare does not exclude another exact EFX and Pareto-optimal allocation.
